description: Stage 2 VT-vs-VF hardware-producible model at 120 Hz (same rate as Stage 1): causal filter + 7 hardware-light features + linear classifier, fixed-point.
rate_choice_rationale: 120 Hz was chosen to EXACTLY match Stage 1's own sample rate (not a multiple of it) --
the maximum possible hardware simplification, letting both stages share one ADC/clock feed
with no divider at all. Nyquist only requires fs >= 80 Hz to represent this filter's own
0.5-40 Hz passband without aliasing; 120 Hz gives a 60 Hz Nyquist frequency, 1.5x the 40 Hz
upper cutoff. Re-validated end to end (not assumed from the 250 Hz result): honest held-out
accuracy, MATLAB fixed-point accuracy, and the full Stage1+Stage2 cascade all matched the

filter.description: Causal (forward-only) 4th-order Butterworth 0.5-40 Hz bandpass, realized as 4 cascaded biquad sections. NOT zero-phase/filtfilt -- streaming-realizable.
filter.sos_note: Each row = [b0 b1 b2 a0 a1 a2] for one biquad; apply sections in sequence via a direct-form-II transposed structure. Coefficients are float64 -- NOT yet quantized to fixed-point (open item, see spec).

signal_format.description: ECG signal quantization. Both quantization points in this pipeline sit immediately after a causal filter has run (the DC blocker, then the main bandpass) and both use the same wide Q5.8 format uniformly -- there is no narrow Q3.8 signal point left in Stage 2's own path; see post_filter_rationale.
post_filter_rationale: The causal bandpass filter has real gain/overshoot that regularly exceeds its OWN input
range -- measured worst case 13.7 across the full 49-record candidate pool while its input
was already bounded to +-8 (Q3.8). Under the original Q3.8-on-both-sides design, this
silently clipped: confirmed actual clipping inside 2 of vfdb/615's 29 real held-out test
windows (peak -10.745, at ~508s into the record). The DC blocker's OWN output has the same
character, independent of its cutoff (swept 0.02-0.5 Hz: worst case stayed 8.9-9.9 the whole
way, ~0.001-0.003% of samples over range regardless). A highpass-order sweep (1st/2nd/3rd)
found order 1 has the LOWEST overshoot of the three, confirming rather than motivating a
change from the original single-pole design. Q5.8 (+-32) is used uniformly at both points
-- one format everywhere a filter has already run, rather than a patchwork of different
widths -- and covers every worst case found with margin. Held-out accuracy measured
identical (0.9510) before and after this fix, but that is not a guarantee for all future
data -- the fix removes a real, previously silent risk rather than relying on it happening
signal_format.truncation_rule: fix() truncation toward zero, then clamp to range
signal_format.baseline_removal: Causal single-pole (1st-order Butterworth) highpass at 0.1 Hz -- replaces a non-causal whole-record median subtraction used in earlier versions of this pipeline, which is impossible for a real streaming device to compute. Verified: identical held-out accuracy (0.9510) to the non-causal version. 0.1 Hz sits a full octave+ below this filter's own 0.5 Hz low corner.
signal_format.invalid_sample_handling: WFDB format-212 dropout sentinel (digital code -2048) detected and linearly interpolated (flat-clamped before the first / after the last valid sample) before quantization.

formulas.derivative_zero_crossings: sign changes in diff(centered), after discarding samples with |value| <= 0.05*mean(|diff(centered)|)
formulas.local_amp_mean: mean over 8 blocks of 0.25s (30 samples each, exact -- covers the full 240-sample window with no leftover, unlike 250 Hz's 496-of-500) of mean(abs(centered)) per block
formulas.local_amp_range: max block mean minus min block mean (same 8 blocks)
formulas.amp_transition: mean absolute difference between consecutive block means

q_format_rationale: Sized from each feature's own observed range across the full 49-record candidate pool
all comfortably inside Q3.8's +-8 range on their own -- narrower than the Q5.8 signal format,
since these are per-window statistics, not raw filter output with overshoot risk. line_length reaches 186 (needs
Q8.8's wider integer headroom, same fraction width as the signal). derivative_zero_crossings
(max 115) and threshold_crossings (max 81) are counts by construction -- Q8.0 needs no
fractional hardware at all, just a wide-enough integer register. The classifier was retrained
on these quantized feature values (not just re-quantized after the fact), and held-out accuracy
was unchanged (0.9510, identical to the float baseline) -- the quantization error is at most
1/256 for the amplitude features and exactly zero for the two counts, which are already integers.
retention_rationale: An ablation on the same held-out set found derivative_zero_crossings contributes no measurable
accuracy change if dropped (0.9608 with or without), while threshold_crossings is load-bearing
(dropping it costs 0.9608 -> 0.9559 accuracy and 0.80 -> 0.77 VT recall) despite having a similarly
small learned coefficient. Both are kept anyway: Stage 1's own base model already computes
zero_crossings and threshold_crossing_count as two of its four features, so the counter/comparator
hardware for this class of feature is already required elsewhere in the design -- keeping both here
reuses that same cheap primitive on a second signal path rather than adding new hardware, so there is
no cost to keeping the one (derivative_zero_crossings) that showed no measured benefit on this test.

classifier.description: StandardScaler + LinearSVC folded offline into one weight-plus-bias linear form -- no runtime division.
classifier.decision_rule: score = dot(features, weight) + bias; predict VF if score > 0, else VT
classifier.why_not_q5_8: 2 of 7 weights underflow to exactly zero at Q5.8's 1/256 resolution (silently dropping those features); Q2.13's finer 1/8192 resolution preserves them. Measured on the same held-out set: float64 accuracy 0.9510, Q2.13 accuracy 0.9510 (delta +0.0000), Q5.8 accuracy 0.9461 (delta -0.0049).

validation.dropped_reason: vfdb/610 has only 4 windows (too small to trust as a test record); cudb/cu18 was the single most consistent poor performer across every diagnostic run in this project.

open_items: Filter (SOS) coefficients are still float64, not quantized -- coefficient quantization can shift pole locations and was not tested here.
RESOLVED (was open in the 250 Hz deliverable): sample rate now exactly matches Stage 1's 120 Hz, so both stages can share one ADC/clock feed.

RESOLVED: the 7 feature values themselves now have explicit, validated Q-formats (see section 4), not just the signal and the classifier weights -- retrained and re-validated end to end with zero accuracy loss.
RESOLVED: baseline removal was a non-causal whole-record median (impossible on a live stream) -- replaced with a causal single-pole 0.1 Hz highpass, verified identical accuracy (0.9510).

RESOLVED: the causal bandpass filter's own gain/overshoot (worst case 13.7 across the pool) was silently clipped by reusing Q3.8 on its output -- confirmed real clipping inside 2 of vfdb/615's actual held-out test windows. The DC blocker's own output has the same character (worst case 8.9-9.9 across a 0.02-0.5 Hz cutoff sweep, ~0.001-0.003% of samples regardless of cutoff). Fixed with a uniform Q5.8 used at both points (not a patchwork of different widths); held-out accuracy unchanged (0.9510). A highpass-order sweep (1st/2nd/3rd) also confirmed the single-pole design has the lowest overshoot of the three, not just the lowest cost.

The 250->120 Hz resampling used here (both in testing and in this validation) is simple linear interpolation, which does not band-limit before downsampling. A live ADC sampling directly at 120 Hz needs its own standard analog anti-aliasing filter ahead of the ADC (true for any sample rate, not unique to 120 Hz) -- this was not an issue in testing (0 mismatches vs Python's properly anti-aliased resampler) because real recorded ECG has little energy above the new Nyquist, but should be designed deliberately, not assumed, in the final hardware front end.
This is a forced binary VT-vs-VF decision with no 'neither' option; Stage 1's gate wakes on non-VT/VF activity a meaningful fraction of the time (71.5% of gate activations in the full cascade test).
